environment: local container; anonymous HTTPS; no cloud project or credentials

limitations: Profile of the committed masked fixture (5 records) re-framed locally as gzip; source_uri names the part the records were selected from; size, sha256 and record/row counts describe the re-framed fixture, not that object, and no content type was served for it.
Profiles one bounded development file; facts do not describe the full snapshot.
Schema, nesting, types, and nullability come from at most 300 leading records; not observing nulls does not prove a field is non-nullable.
Field paths use '.' for object members and '[]' for array elements; unusual keys are JSON-quoted, and abstract_inverted_index word keys are collapsed into one map value path.

Decoded bytes include the EOF probe. Limits bound consumed bytes and JSON structure, not gzip's internal read-ahead or exact Python heap usage. The deadline is cooperative and cannot interrupt a native call.
LOCAL bounded inspection from a sandbox container; not cloud or enterprise evidence.
One JSONL/Parquet Works pair was downloaded whole; every other part is described by the manifests and the full listing only, and one large Parquet part was read footer-only.

The JSONL schema is sampled from the first 300 records of the pair; the line count comes from the drain, and every line was parsed by the script for fidelity. The Parquet schema is exact for the profiled files only.
Gzip member structure is known for the downloaded pair only; for large parts it is UNKNOWN.
The deletion ledger is above the per-object cap: only a 65,536-byte prefix was read, so its row count is unknown and 'cumulative' is not proven.
Rights and cadence are quoted from the snapshot's own LICENSE.txt, README.txt and RELEASE_NOTES.txt only; help.openalex.org was not read.
The TLS peer is the sandbox's agent proxy, so integrity rests on matching sizes, record counts, S3 CRC64NVME and ETags, not on the TLS certificate of S3 itself.
Profiles one bounded development file; facts do not describe the full snapshot.
Schema, nesting, types, and nullability come from at most 300 leading records; not observing nulls does not prove a field is non-nullable.
Field paths use '.' for object members and '[]' for array elements; unusual keys are JSON-quoted, and abstract_inverted_index word keys are collapsed into one map value path.

Decoded bytes include the EOF probe. Limits bound consumed bytes and JSON structure, not gzip's internal read-ahead or exact Python heap usage. The deadline is cooperative and cannot interrupt a native call.
The file was drained to EOF after the sample: row_count counts newline-terminated lines beyond the sample without parsing them, and gzip CRC32/ISIZE were verified at the member end.
Profiles one bounded development file; facts do not describe the full snapshot.
Schema, nullability, row and row-group counts, codecs, and statistics availability come from the exact Parquet footer.
Parquet values were not read (footer_only); schema, nullability, counts and codecs are exact footer facts.
Types are PyArrow's interpretation of the Parquet schema.

Footer byte/Thrift and schema/work guards apply; the dictionary-expansion and batch-byte guards were not applied because no values were read (footer_only). Footer declarations are not a hard native-memory sandbox, and cooperative deadlines cannot interrupt native Arrow calls.
Bytes were spooled to a temporary local file, deleted after profiling, because the Parquet footer is at the end of the file.

profiled_pair.rule: latest updated_date pair with both files <= 2,000,000 bytes and >= 1,000 records
